title: Family name banner in cross-stitch
subtitle: A personalised surname in a banner-style frame with corner motifs
excerpt: A family name banner is a personalised cross-stitch piece in a rectangular frame with a decorative border and corner motifs. The surname is stitched in a 9-stitch-tall Roman-style uppercase alphabet. The fabric area is 110 stitches wide by 70 stitches tall on 14-count Aida, which accommodates up to twelve letters. Finished size is about 20 x 13 cm.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. Name sampler tradition in British needlework documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

content.text: A family name banner is a personalised piece that fits a surname of up to twelve letters in a 9-stitch-tall Roman uppercase alphabet inside a bordered rectangle on 14-count
. The border is a simple two-colour repeating vine pattern with a squared corner section. Small motifs, a pair of leaves or hearts, sit in each corner inside the border. The

colours are a single contrast for the text and a two-tone green for the vine border. This piece requires planning the letter spacing before stitching: count the total letter width, adjust, and confirm it fits the inner frame before starting.

attrs.heading: Adapting for your surname
attrs.text: The template fits up to twelve letters with 1-stitch gaps. For a shorter name, centre it in the frame and leave blank stitches either side. For a name longer than twelve letters: reduce the letter height to 7 stitches (the same font at smaller scale) or use a wider piece of fabric. Do not stitch a name at a size where the letters run into the border.

items.name: 14-count Aida, cream or natural linen
items.substitutions: Natural linen Aida gives a traditional sampler feel

items.name: DMC floss for text
items.qty: 1 or 2 skeins depending on surname length: navy 823 or burgundy 814
items.substitutions: Any strong contrast to the Aida colour

items.name: Rectangular frame
items.substitutions: A large hoop also works for stitching but frame for display

content.text: Plan the letter spacing on graph paper or the chart template first. Count the total stitch width and mark the centre letter. Confirm the total fits inside the inner border width before putting needle to fabric.
Stitch the four corner motifs of the border first, then work each border side from a corner toward the centre. This gives the corner placement priority and absorbs any repeat arithmetic in the sides.
Stitch the surname from the centre letter outward once the full border is complete.
Add any back-stitch detail (a fine line within the letter serifs, if using a serif variant of the alphabet) last.

Wash gently and press face-down. A traditional sampler frame, dark wood with a cream or olive mount, suits the style. This piece is a good candidate for framing under museum glass to protect the floss colours.
The house name sampler in this sub-category uses the same alphabet and a similar bordered layout. The house name is the centrepiece instead of a family surname.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
